overview:
The target result is a deterministic fixed-tape machine that multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time, where $\kappa = 2^{-182}$. Since $(\lg n)^{1-\kappa}/\lg n$ tends to zero, this is asymptotically faster than $n\log n$, and so it disproves the [$n\log n$ optimality conjecture](n-log-n-conjecture.md) within the [fixed-tape model](fixed-tape-model.md). The result matters because it shows that $n\log n$ is not the optimal order of growth for multiplication in this model.

The route runs through eight parts. The first sets out [running-time cost](running-time-cost.md), [arrays](array.md) and [exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md), which reduces to [convolution](convolution.md). The second develops the [linear algebra](linear-algebra-basics.md) and the [discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) that turns convolution into a pointwise product. The third introduces [linear networks](linear-network-frames.md) and splits integers into [radix digits](radix-digit-convolution.md), so that multiplication becomes a convolution of short coefficients. The fourth adds [congruences](congruence-modulo.md), the [Chinese remainder theorem](chinese-remainder-theorem.md) and the [polynomial ring modulo $y^r+1$](polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.md), in which a wrap-around becomes a sign change. The fifth builds [subset-intersection networks](subset-intersection-network.md), which move values while restoring scratch storage. The sixth turns them into the [address interchange](address-interchange.md) and [simultaneous butterfly layers](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md). The seventh gives the [rank-saving recursion](rank-saving-recursion.md) and the [transform layout](transform-layout.md), and collects the [cost table](cost-table.md). The eighth packs signed coefficients ([signed packing](signed-packing.md)), recovers them exactly ([exact coefficient recovery](recovery-and-error.md)), and combines the pieces in the [main theorem](main-theorem.md).

parts.title: Background: numbers, arrays and cost
parts.intro: This part fixes the vocabulary of the argument: growth rates, the cost of a machine computation, and the arrays whose entries carry addresses. It also introduces exact integer multiplication and its reduction to [convolution](convolution.md). Every later part depends on these notions.

parts.title: Linear algebra and the Fourier transform
parts.intro: The argument works with linear maps on arrays, so this part recalls [linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md) and the operators built from them, including projections, eigenvalues and contractions. The [discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) is then introduced as the map that turns convolution into a pointwise product. Both are needed for the linear networks and transforms that follow.

parts.title: Linear networks and radix-digit convolution
parts.intro: This part introduces [cyclic shifts](cyclic-shift.md) and [butterflies](butterfly.md), the local steps of a Fourier-type transform, and the linear networks that realise them. It then splits each integer into [radix digits](radix-digit-convolution.md), so that multiplication becomes a convolution of short coefficients. [Carry propagation](carry-propagation.md) turns the recovered coefficients back into a binary string.

parts.title: Rings, congruences and fast multiplication
parts.intro: Modular arithmetic and the [Chinese remainder theorem](chinese-remainder-theorem.md) let a transform length be chosen as a product of coprime moduli. [Rings](ring.md) and the [polynomial ring modulo $y^r+1$](polynomial-ring-mod-yr-plus-1.md) supply the algebra in which the synthetic transforms act. The [Schönhage–Strassen method](schonhage-strassen.md) and the [$n\log n$ conjecture](n-log-n-conjecture.md) are introduced here, because the main result is stated against them.

parts.title: Subset-intersection networks
parts.intro: A [subset-intersection network](subset-intersection-network.md) is a linear network on three-element subsets that exchanges two banks of values while restoring its scratch wires. This part builds its [bilinear form](bilinear-form.md), its [subspace labels](subspace-labels.md) and the complex version with [Gaussian dyadic](gaussian-dyadics.md) scalars. These networks are the device that moves values inside an array.

parts.title: Tape procedures and address interchange
parts.intro: A [tape procedure](tape-procedure.md) moves the contents of a machine's tapes in a bounded number of passes. This part turns the networks above into the [address interchange](address-interchange.md), the [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md) and the [transform round](transform-round.md). It also covers [stable radix sorting](stable-radix-sort.md), which the record moves rely on.

parts.title: Recursion and transform layout
parts.intro: The [rank-saving recursion](rank-saving-recursion.md) splits each call into smaller calls on streams whose volume shrinks, so that the cost falls by a strict factor per level. A [transform layout](transform-layout.md) places the selected bits of all axes in consecutive chunks, and [Bluestein's identity](bluestein-chirp-identity.md) rewrites the middle transform as a cyclic convolution. This part also assembles the [cost table](cost-table.md) whose terms are bounded later.

parts.title: Packing, recovery and the bound
parts.intro: Coefficients are packed as [signed blocks](signed-packing.md) in one integer, multiplied with the [established multiplier](established-multiplier.md), and recovered by rounding. The error analysis in [exact coefficient recovery](recovery-and-error.md) shows that each computed coefficient lies within one half of its true integer value. The final part combines these pieces in the [main theorem](main-theorem.md).
